title: Permanence of proper, separated, finite type, finitely presented morphisms and of immersions
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. (a) If $f$ and $g$ are proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], so is $g\circ f$. (b) If $f$ is proper, then for every morphism $Y'\to Y$ the base change $X\times_YY'\to Y'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is proper; likewise if $f$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], so is its base change. (c) A closed immersion is proper. (d) If $f$ and $g$ are of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated) [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], so is $g\circ f$. (e) If $f$ and $g$ are separated (resp. locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], resp. immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]), so is $g\circ f$. (f) If $g\circ f$ is locally of finite type, so is $f$.
